targetPlans.observableAction: select Compute Engine GKE Cloud Run or Cloud Run functions from control runtime and operations needs.
targetPlans.countRationale: For “select Compute Engine GKE Cloud Run or Cloud Run functions from control runtime and operations needs.”, 7 independent decisions remain: Determine which execution products support the required GPU or TPU while preserving the workload's packaging model. Choose GKE only when the workload needs Kubernetes scheduling, controllers, or multi-service container orchestration. Identify when a small event handler should use Cloud Run functions rather than a general container service. Compare infrastructure ownership across Compute Engine, GKE, and Cloud Run before selecting a compute product. Select Compute Engine when the application requires guest OS, kernel, boot-file, or machine-level administration. Test whether a continuously running stateful process fits the selected managed compute contract. Choose Cloud Run for a stateless HTTP or gRPC container when server and cluster administration are not required. The rejected proposals do not add another material boundary: workload-requirement-transfer — A generic whole-workload transfer would only recombine the retained accelerator, orchestration, function, operations, kernel, stateful-process, and stateless-service boundaries without adding a new product property.

droppedSlotRationales.google-cloud-associate-cloud-engineer:co: A generic whole-workload transfer would only recombine the retained accelerator, orchestration, function, operations, kernel, stateful-process, and stateless-service boundaries without adding a new product property.

targetPlans.ownershipRationale: Retained in the accepted foundations remap for setup, identity, solution planning, or infrastructure delivery.

targetPlans.observableAction: match execution model to state and request lifetime.
targetPlans.countRationale: For “match execution model to state and request lifetime.”, 4 independent decisions remain: Match an event-triggered unit of work to a function, service, or job by invocation and completion semantics. Determine whether an HTTP operation can complete within the configured Cloud Run request timeout. Classify a Cloud Run container as a service or job from its process contract. Decide which state must move outside a Cloud Run instance before the workload can scale or restart safely. The rejected proposals do not add another material boundary: lifetime-requirement-transfer — The retained timeout, service-versus-job, event-entry, and state-externalization items already name the exact execution-contract change that causes transfer; a generic lifetime transfer repeats them.

droppedSlotRationales.google-cloud-associate-cloud-engineer:co: The retained timeout, service-versus-job, event-entry, and state-externalization items already name the exact execution-contract change that causes transfer; a generic lifetime transfer repeats them.

targetPlans.ownershipRationale: Retained in the accepted foundations remap for setup, identity, solution planning, or infrastructure delivery.

targetPlans.observableAction: select Cloud Storage Persistent Disk Filestore or database storage from access protocol and durability.
targetPlans.countRationale: For “select Cloud Storage Persistent Disk Filestore or database storage from access protocol and durability.”, 7 independent decisions remain: Separate durability from availability when evaluating a storage requirement. Recognize when query, transaction, indexing, or record-update needs require a database instead of file, block, or object storage. Change the storage topology when the tolerated zone or region failure changes. Reject Local SSD for data that must survive VM stop, deletion, or host failure. Choose Cloud Storage when applications exchange immutable or append-oriented objects through an object API. Choose Persistent Disk when a Compute Engine workload needs durable block storage attached to a VM. Choose Filestore when multiple clients require a managed shared NFS filesystem. The rejected proposals do not add another material boundary: multiwriter-protocol-boundary — For this target, concurrent file access resolves through the retained Filestore shared-NFS choice; a second multiwriter label does not introduce a distinct supported storage protocol decision.

droppedSlotRationales.google-cloud-associate-cloud-engineer:da: For this target, concurrent file access resolves through the retained Filestore shared-NFS choice; a second multiwriter label does not introduce a distinct supported storage protocol decision.

targetPlans.ownershipRationale: Retained in the accepted foundations remap for setup, identity, solution planning, or infrastructure delivery.

targetPlans.observableAction: select a managed data service from query and consistency requirements.
targetPlans.countRationale: For “select a managed data service from query and consistency requirements.”, 8 independent decisions remain: Use the required read and transaction consistency as a hard boundary when choosing a managed database. Classify the workload's primary model as relational rows, documents, or wide-column key ranges before comparing services. Distinguish Cloud SQL vertical instance scaling from databases designed for horizontal scale. Choose Bigtable only when sustained low-latency, high-throughput key-based access matches its data model. Separate online application transactions from large analytical scans when choosing between operational databases and BigQuery. Match required query operations to the interfaces a managed data service actually exposes. Choose between Cloud SQL and Spanner from relational compatibility, scale, and distribution requirements. Re-run data-service selection when one decisive requirement changes instead of preserving the incumbent product by default. The rejected proposals do not add another material boundary: operations-burden-comparison — All compared products are managed and the proposed item lacked a specific service-management duty that would change selection beyond the retained data model, query, consistency, scale, and workload boundaries.

droppedSlotRationales.google-cloud-associate-cloud-engineer:da: All compared products are managed and the proposed item lacked a specific service-management duty that would change selection beyond the retained data model, query, consistency, scale, and workload boundaries.

targetPlans.observableAction: express resource dependencies identities and configuration declaratively.
targetPlans.countRationale: For “express resource dependencies identities and configuration declaratively.”, 5 independent decisions remain: Represent service API enablement as a dependency when a Terraform resource cannot be created before its API is active. Diagnose a Terraform plan or apply failure caused by a missing resource dependency rather than by invalid provider credentials. Create Terraform dependencies through expression references when one resource consumes another resource's value. Configure Terraform to use an approved application identity without embedding a long-lived service-account key in configuration. Expose only the resource attributes a consuming Terraform module needs, then reference those outputs explicitly. Every reviewed proposal changes a separate documented condition, so none is removed.
targetPlans.ownershipRationale: Retained in the accepted foundations remap for setup, identity, solution planning, or infrastructure delivery.

targetPlans.observableAction: parameterize environment-specific values without duplicating resource definitions.
targetPlans.countRationale: For “parameterize environment-specific values without duplicating resource definitions.”, 4 independent decisions remain: Define a Terraform input variable for a value callers must choose per deployment. Use locals for internal expression reuse and outputs for values intentionally exposed outside a module. Factor repeated infrastructure into a module when deployments share resource structure but vary through a bounded input contract. Change a parameter's ownership when a once-variable value becomes an invariant or a derived implementation detail. The rejected proposals do not add another material boundary: environment-sensitive-value-path — Caller inputs, module locals, outputs, module reuse, and ownership transfer already exhaust the concrete destinations for environment-sensitive values; the generic path adds no sixth Terraform construct.

rangeReconciliation.decision: Patternly keeps the canonical 50-item practice simulation because it is the documented lower bound and exactly realizes all approximate domain weights; 60 is a valid future form size but is not needed for feasibility.

practiceForm.objectiveAllocationRule: Within each domain, cover every objective represented by eligible authored items before filling remaining positions; no objective-level provider weight is claimed because Google documents none.
practiceForm.responseFormatRule: Use only the certification family's existing supported choice interaction. The provider's documented multiple-select format is evidence of a fidelity gap, not an active or conditional candidate interaction.

providerFormatGap.implication: Provider-faithful simulation remains blocked; do not expand the runtime interaction contract in this correction.

practiceForm.selectionRule: Select unique eligible slots without semantic-fingerprint reuse, preserve 20/30/30/20 domain allocation, and prevent one target from occupying more than 20% of its domain unless inventory makes the form impossible.
practiceForm.behaviorBoundary: Do not emulate or claim undocumented navigation, answer-change, flagging, navigator, timeout, or scored/unscored behavior.

crossTrackOverlapRules: Shared concepts require track-specific context and transfer boundary; active item identity cannot be shared across tracks.
